nodes.label: Model Collapse as Change of Scaling Laws
nodes.author: Elvis Dohmatob, Yunzhen Feng, Pu Yang, Francois Charton, Julia Kempe
nodes.rationale: Theoretical framework analyzing how scaling laws change when synthetic data contaminates training corpus, discovering decay phenomena and grokking effects

nodes.label: Neural Scaling Laws
nodes.rationale: Empirically observed power-law relationships where test error falls off as power of training data size, model size, and compute

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Contamination
nodes.rationale: AI-generated data increasingly populating web and training corpora, often indistinguishable from real data, causing distribution shift

nodes.label: Tail Cutting Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Mechanism where synthetic data generation cuts off low-probability tail of heavy-tailed distribution, leading to peaked distributions

nodes.label: Tail Narrowing Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Mechanism where synthetic data generation narrows tail exponent of heavy-tailed distribution through temperature scaling and truncation

nodes.label: Double Scaling Law
nodes.rationale: New scaling law showing test error as sum of two power-law terms dependent on both current training data and generator training data

nodes.label: Triplet Scaling Law for Memory-Limited Models
nodes.rationale: Scaling law for associative memory models showing dependence on embedding dimension and algorithm-specific exponent

nodes.label: Grokking Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Mitigation strategy where mixing AI-generated data with small amount of clean data introduces plateau followed by continued error decrease

nodes.label: Zipf Distribution
nodes.rationale: Heavy-tailed power-law distribution ubiquitous in natural data including word frequencies, biological data, financial data

nodes.label: Llama2 Model Collapse Experiments
nodes.rationale: Large-scale experiments fine-tuning Llama2-7B on Wikitext-103 dataset to validate theoretical predictions about model collapse

nodes.label: Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) Task
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic task used to validate model collapse theory with transformer models, demonstrating loss of skills phenomenon

nodes.label: Model Collapse Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Central phenomenon where AI-generated data loses heavy-tailed distribution properties, causing downstream models to plateau in performance rather than continue scaling improvements.

nodes.label: Tail Cutting Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Deliberate or implicit truncation of low-probability outcomes in AI generation (via top-k, top-p) or finite sampling bias, which removes rare skills from training distribution.

nodes.label: Theorem 2.1: Scaling Law with Tail Cutting
nodes.rationale: Establishes that test error scales as min(T, k^β)^(-(β-1)/β) when training on tail-cut data, showing performance plateaus once T ≳ k^β.

nodes.label: Hutter LLM Model
nodes.rationale: Simplified theoretical model of LLM that predicts next skill i given previous skill, used as foundation for analyzing scaling laws and model collapse.

nodes.label: Theorem 2.4: Multi-generation Collapse
nodes.rationale: Characterizes when model collapse occurs across n generations: collapse iff n ≫ (T₀/T)^c, showing cumulative degradation with iterations.

nodes.label: Grokking Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Delayed learning effect where test error plateaus initially when mixing clean and synthetic data, then resumes improvement—predicted by theory and observed empirically.

nodes.label: Theorem 3.2: Grokking with Tail Cutting
nodes.rationale: Proves grokking occurs when mixing π-fraction clean data with (1-π) synthetic data; early stage shows no benefit, later stage recovers unpolluted scaling law.

nodes.label: Hutter++ Model (Probabilistic)
nodes.rationale: Extension of Hutter model to probabilistic setting with conditional distributions p(j|i), modeling next-token prediction in autoregressive LLMs.

nodes.label: Theorem 4.1: Hutter++ Scaling Law
nodes.rationale: Shows Hutter++ achieves same scaling law as classical Hutter model: E_test ≍ T^(-c) where c = min(1-1/β, 1/2).

nodes.label: Theorem 4.2: Model Collapse in Probabilistic Setting
nodes.rationale: Extends model collapse analysis to probabilistic Hutter++: E_test ≲ T^(-c) + k^(-βc), showing tail-cutting effect persists in autoregressive models.

nodes.label: Capacity-Limited Memory Model
nodes.rationale: Finite-memory associative memory model with embedding dimension d, extending Hutter to account for model capacity constraints.

nodes.label: Theorem 5.1: Triplet Scaling Law
nodes.rationale: Establishes three-way scaling: E_test ≍ T^(-(1-1/β)) + d^(-c_q) + k^(-(β-1)), showing interplay of sample size, capacity, and tail-cutting.

nodes.label: FreshWiki Dataset
nodes.rationale: Empirical validation uses simplified LLM models on synthetic Zipf data; demonstrates predicted scaling law decay and grokking phenomena.

nodes.label: GCD Transformer Experiments
nodes.rationale: Sequence-to-sequence transformer trained to predict greatest common divisor; intermediate complexity between toy models and full LLMs, validates skill emergence and collapse.

nodes.label: Llama2-7B Finetuning Experiments
nodes.rationale: Large-scale validation on real LLM using Wikitext-103; demonstrates model collapse across generations and grokking effect with data mixing.

nodes.label: Scaling Law Decay (Core Finding)
nodes.rationale: Central result: when training on AI-generated data with tail-cut distribution, test error plateaus rather than continuing to improve with more data.

nodes.label: Skill Emergence and Disappearance
nodes.rationale: Models trained on clean data learn new skills (GCDs) in bursts; models trained on AI data plateau and never learn skills beyond initial generation.

nodes.label: Finite Sampling Bias
nodes.rationale: Implicit tail-cutting from finite training set size T₀; support of empirical distribution is {i | p_i ≥ C/T₀}, inducing effective rank cutoff k.

nodes.label: Tail Narrowing (Alternative to Cutting)
nodes.rationale: AI-generated data has long-tail distribution but with smaller exponent β' < β; results in slower decay rate rather than plateau.

nodes.label: Theorem 3.1: Acquiring Missing Tail
nodes.rationale: Sharp phase transition: curating tail data at rank N ≈ k recovers scaling, but N >> k makes curation worthless; precise targeting required.

nodes.label: Corollary 3.3: Benefits of Mixing AI Data
nodes.rationale: When T_real << k^β, mixing AI data helps: E_test ≍ (T_real + T_AI)^(-(1-1/β)) + k^(-(β-1)), showing AI data can boost performance in data-scarce regime.

nodes.label: Watermarking for Synthetic Data Detection
nodes.rationale: Proposed mitigation: watermark synthetic data to distinguish from human-authored content, enabling selective filtering during training.

nodes.label: Data Curation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Strategic acquisition of tail data at precise rank k (within factor 1+o(1)) can recover scaling; requires careful targeting rather than arbitrary curation.

nodes.label: Corollary 2.2: Finite Initial Sample Size
nodes.rationale: When AI generator trained on T₀ samples, effective tail-cutting rank k ≍ T₀^(1/β); loss of scaling follows same pattern as explicit tail-cutting.

nodes.label: Universality of Scaling Law Decay
nodes.rationale: Model collapse mechanisms apply across different architectures (Hutter, Hutter++, capacity-limited memory); demonstrates fundamental nature of phenomenon.

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Age Challenge
nodes.rationale: Emerging era where training corpora increasingly contain AI-generated data; scaling laws cease to persist, requiring new strategies for model development.
